A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, Table 1, Figure 1, and complete appendices. The retained appendices can be matched despite renumbering; v3 adds Appendices F and I.

before.justification: v2 Appendix A reports original numerical simulations comparing fixed and adaptive FTRL regularization across dimensions, with outcomes plotted in Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations and their reported outcomes in Appendix A and Figure 1.

M1.justification: v2 discusses doubling intervals for constant-step OMD. v3 Appendix F introduces AMD+, which selects a rate-dependent regularizer for each doubling interval. The primary adaptive FTRL procedure in Section 3 remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic online linear-loss construction on lp-balls across dimensions. The new theoretical appendices introduce no additional evaluated datasets, tasks, or scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same four FTRL variants: phi_2, phi_p, and adaptive regularization with either the theorem's switching threshold or t0 = 2d. AMD+ is not empirically evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains T = 40, L = 1, p = 10, the dimension sweep, regret metric, step-size schedules, and numerical projection procedure.

E4.justification: The dimension-dependent comparison and sensitivity check using t0 = 2d are present in both versions. No additional empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies appear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the simulation. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1 contains the identical plot, and Appendix A retains the same findings about dimension dependence and switching thresholds. No empirical result entries or numerical outcomes change.

T1.justification: New Appendix F adds Theorem F.2 and a proof for adapting OMD to an envelope of regret rates. New Appendix I adds an impossibility theorem and supporting propositions for non-separable regularizers under sign/permutation invariance and consistency under zero padding, restricted to constant step sizes. Appendix E.4 also revises Lipschitz-scaling factors in an existing derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: adaptive FTRL achieves anytime optimality, fixed separable regularizers cannot, and sufficiently high-dimensional bandit problems preclude sublinear regret. The added appendix results do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Remark 4.10 now explains how universality can accommodate changing regret rates through different regularizers across intervals. Appendix F discusses the additional logarithmic factors and larger constants relative to Theorem 3.1. The unrestricted non-separable case remains open.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same Google Colab CPU execution, approximately five-minute runtime, scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP, and Appendix B update formulas. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 46 cited works remain. Remark 4.10 and new Appendix F expand the relationship to Sridharan's universality result, explaining its extension to changing rates and the continuing relevance of the paper's direct construction.

P1.justification: v3 systematically corrects theorem, proposition, lemma, and appendix references, adds two appendices, and removes the acknowledgments and funding section. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Removing the first-page conference footer and acknowledgments produces limited text and reference reflow. Table 1 and Figure 1 retain their visual structure; no figures or tables are added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: Appendices F and I offer potentially valuable theoretical extensions, and corrected cross-references improve navigation. However, F.2 applies F.1 to doubling intervals starting at length 1 despite F.1's horizon restriction, while I.2 incorrectly uses 1/ceil(a) >= 1/a in its step-size derivation. These unresolved proof issues make the net quality benefit of the substantive additions uncertain.
